gen_risks.description: Delay in execution of Trust Deed and adoption of Project Operations Manual could postpone CRF establishment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set internal legal deadline; conduct weekly review; obtain early sign‑off from Ministry of Finance and SBP before project start.
gen_risks.evidence: Conditions 5.01(a) and 5.01(b) require the Trust Deed executed and State Bank adopt the Project Operations Manual before effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Inaccurate climate risk modelling may lead to improper trigger thresholds and delayed or inappropriate disbursement.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contract reputable modelling firms, conduct peer review, update models annually and validate against historical flood events.
gen_risks.evidence: Catastrophe modelling will be undertaken; risk modelling will be the basis for pricing and triggers.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient capital if CRF scope expands beyond flood coverage without additional financing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include a contingency financing clause, pre‑negotiate donor bridge loans, and maintain a reserve within the CRF.
gen_risks.evidence: Enhancing the scope of climate risks covered by the CRF may require additional capital; any additional financing subject to approval.

gen_risks.description: Funding shortfall for parametric insurance premium could prevent back‑stop activation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Secure a multi‑year insurance contract; earmark grant and investment income in an escrow account for premiums.
gen_risks.evidence: Insurance premium budget US$26 million, half from GSFF grant and half from CRF investment income; annual decision by Oversight Committee.

gen_risks.description: Increased use of fertilizers and pesticides from agritech loans may cause localized environmental degradation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed environmental safeguards in loan terms, promote integrated pest management, and monitor chemical use via MIS.
gen_risks.evidence: Cumulative impacts may increase use of fertilizers, pesticides, worsening air quality and soil contamination; impacts localized.

gen_risks.description: Low uptake by micro‑finance providers due to mandatory partnership with ATCs could limit liquidity flow.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance and incentives to MFPs for ATC partnership; streamline AFIC selection; offer capacity‑building grants.
gen_risks.evidence: MFPs that avail the IAL product will have to partner with at least one ATC selected under the AFIC.

gen_risks.description: Failure to achieve 55% women beneficiary target could undermine gender‑equity objectives.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce gender allocation clause with penalty (higher borrowing cost), monitor gender disbursement quarterly, and provide gender‑focused training.
gen_risks.evidence: Ensure at least 55% of beneficiaries of CRF liquidity are women; MFPs pay higher borrowing cost if deviation.

gen_risks.description: Reliance on third‑party data providers may compromise trigger data quality and timeliness.
gen_risks.mitigation: Contract multiple data sources, establish a data validation protocol, and include service‑level agreements for timely delivery.
gen_risks.evidence: Data required to evaluate triggers will be provided by third‑party service providers (e.g., credit rating agencies, flood risk modelling firms).

gen_risks.description: Ongoing macro‑economic crisis could erode sector liquidity, reducing effectiveness of CRF support.
gen_risks.mitigation: Build a CRF capital buffer, coordinate with fiscal authorities for stabilization measures, and diversify funding sources.
gen_risks.evidence: Impact of shocks exacerbated by macroeconomic crisis since 2019; erosion of liquidity and capital of MFBs.

gen_risks.description: Oversight Committee may delay strategic decisions such as securing insurance, affecting timely fund deployment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Define clear decision timelines (e.g., within 10 days of trigger) and assign delegated authority for interim actions.
gen_risks.evidence: Oversight Committee will be tasked with strategic decisions, such as making a determination on whether to secure parametric insurance.

gen_risks.description: Legal restriction on amending the Trust Deed without consent could hinder necessary project adjustments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Include a pre‑approved amendment clause for project‑related changes and obtain a written consent framework in advance.
gen_risks.evidence: Trust Deed shall not be amended, abrogated, or waived without prior written consent of the Association.

gen_risks.description: Disbursement delays due to IFR reporting and pooled‑account setup could slow liquidity provision.
gen_risks.mitigation: Automate IFR submission, set an internal 30‑day review window, and provide staff training on reporting procedures.
gen_risks.evidence: Disbursement will be report based; each IFR submitted to Bank within 45 days; pooled account front‑loaded for CRF capitalization.

gen_risks.description: Weaknesses in M&E data quality may affect monitoring of project outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen MIS, conduct regular data audits, and provide capacity‑building for M&E staff.
gen_risks.evidence: SBP will work to further strengthen its M&E including the quality of data collection.

gen_risks.description: Misalignment of insurance trigger with actual flood impacts could result in insufficient payout.
gen_risks.mitigation: Align trigger parameters with government emergency declarations and sector‑impact thresholds; run joint simulation exercises annually.
gen_risks.evidence: Two independent triggers: one activates CRF, another unlocks insurance payout; thresholds detailed in POM.

gen_risks.description: Increasing frequency of extreme floods may exceed the CRF’s capital capacity.
gen_risks.mitigation: Perform periodic stress testing, consider scaling up CRF capital or adding additional reinsurance arrangements.
gen_risks.evidence: CRF will only provide support in instances the flooding event is classified as ‘large’ or ‘extreme’; climate risks increasing.

gt_risks.description: Political and Governance risk is Substantial. The political context in Pakistan remains fluid. However, there has been significant decline in political uncertainty and associated policy instability in recent months, especially in the backdrop of the general elections. Given that a new government took the helm recently and the fact that policy priorities are still being defined, political risks, in particular in the context of the project, remain substantial.
gt_risks.mitigation: In the implementation stage, the risks will be mitigated through frequent monitoring and oversight.

gt_risks.description: Macroeconomic risk is High. While fiscal consolidation measures have supported short-term stabilization, macroeconomic risks remain high amid a high debt burden (72 percent of GDP), heavy financial sector exposure to government debt, large external financing needs, weak confidence, and little progress with structural reforms. Significant risks include potential worsening of external conditions, further natural disasters, and a slowdown or reversals in policy adjustment.
gt_risks.mitigation: Risks are partly mitigated by government commitment to implementation of reforms under the ongoing International Monetary Fund program, World Bank support to structural policy reforms in the fiscal and power sectors, strong government commitment to the reforms supported by the operation, and the availability of dedicated World Bank technical assistance to implement key reforms.
